what: A single thick brush stroke that starts at the top left, wraps once around the screen and curls inward becomes the page transition curtain. Pressing a link to another page draws the stroke to 85% in 1 second, and from .25s its thickness swells from 5% → 30% of the screen to cover it and move on. On the opened page it waits .4s covered at 30% thickness, then retracts toward the end over 1.25s while thinning to 5%

options.cover: Cover duration after pressing (seconds), default 1 — the next page is called only after full cover, so the transition is delayed by this much
options.reveal: Length (sec) of the open page peeling away, default 1.25
options.delay: Wait (seconds) before it clears on the opened page, default 0.4
options.thick: Thickness when covering (% of screen), default 30
options.[data-fx-part=stroke]: When changing the brush stroke shape — put inside one with viewBox 1000×1000 <path> With one <svg>. If none, default spiral brush stroke

use: <body data-fx="brush-page-swipe"> — For frequent app-like page swiping, use data-fx-brush-page-swipe="cover: 0.4; reveal: 0.5; delay: 0"

from.where: shared.js brush-stroke transition (barba 2.10.3 default — leave 1s drawSVG 0→85% · from .25s stroke width 5→30% over .75s, enter 1s then at 1.25s 100% 100%·5%, the first open is the same reveal after .4s)

note: The original overlaps two Barba pages when navigating (the old page is covered over 1 second and the new page turns on in 1 second). Our part uses normal navigation, so it loads the new page after covering, and the opened page starts covered and then clears. Sites that use Barba just copy over the leave and enter values. Lines are drawn with stroke-dasharray instead of drawSVG, so it runs without the plugin
